- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., > -0.16 or multiple consecutive negative values), model tends to overcorrect downward — reduce forecast bias by 5–10% relative to recent highs.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+0.20 in sentiment or +1.5+ in price), model often overshoots downward — cap forecast decline to 10–15% below peak for 3–5 days.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive — add 0.5–1.0 to forecast mean for first 5 days.
- When sentiment shows strong upward momentum (e.g., >+0.20), model often fails to capture momentum — increase forecast slope by 10–20% for next 3–7 days.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias — if 3+ consecutive days show downward trend, forecast should not drop below 10% below 14-day moving average unless sentiment confirms strong bearish signal.
- For sentiment history with alternating +/– swings, model tends to lag — forecast should be adjusted upward by 0.5–1.0 for 2–4 days after sentiment shifts from negative to positive.
